title: Finance & Legal — Integrated Budgeting, Procurement, Contracts, and Revenue Recognition Operational Playbook (Q3 2025)
author: Lina Martinez
body:
Overview

This playbook documents Redwood Inference's end-to-end operational practices for annual budgeting and rolling forecasts, procurement requests and approvals, contract intake and lifecycle, and revenue recognition & billing policies. It is intended as the single-source operational reference for Finance, Legal, Procurement, and partnering teams (Product, Eng, Sales, and Customer Success).

Objectives

- Provide a clear, repeatable budgeting and forecasting cadence with owners and deliverables.
- Standardize procurement intake, approval thresholds, and vendor onboarding steps.
- Define contract intake checklist, review SLAs, and signature routing for customer/provider contracts.
- Document revenue recognition and billing rules aligned to ASC 606 principles used at Redwood.
- Reduce cycle time for approvals while maintaining control and auditability.

Scope

Applies to: all Redwood employees and contractors initiating budgets, procurement requests, commercial contracts, customer billing, or revenue reporting for hosted, dedicated, or private products.

Roles & Ownership

- Finance (Owner): Lina Martinez — overall owner of budgeting, forecasting, billing, and revenue recognition policies.
- Legal (Owner): Omar Singh — contract review, risk exceptions, and compliance guidance.
- Procurement (Process Lead): Rachel Park — vendor onboarding, PO issuance, supplier contracts.
- Revenue Ops: Ben Carter — billing operations, invoicing cadence, billing disputes.
- Requesting Team Lead: engineering/product/sales managers — submit requests and provide business justification.

Annual Budgeting and Forecasting

Cadence and Deliverables

1. Annual Budget cycle (Oct–Dec):
   - Finance issues budget templates and targets (by cost center) on Oct 1.
   - Department submissions due Nov 15 (revenue, headcount, opex/capex requests, contract commitments).
   - Exec review & consolidation Nov 20 – Dec 10.
   - Board-approved budget published by Dec 20.

2. Rolling Forecast (monthly):
   - Forecast window: 12 months rolling, updated monthly.
   - Each month teams submit updated headcount and major contract changes by 3rd business day.
   - Finance consolidates and publishes variance analysis by 10th business day.

Templates & Artifacts

- Budget template (Finance Drive): revenue model, hiring plan, OPEX by category, capital requests, assumptions sheet.
- Forecast workbook: month-by-month P&L reforecast, cash runway, variance commentary.

Budgeting Principles & Constraints

- Headcount requests > $50k annual run-rate require VP approval and headcount committee review.
- Capital purchases > $100k require CFO approval and capital justification (payback, TCO).
- New recurring vendor commitments require Procurement intake and Legal review before PO or contract signature.

Procurement & Vendor Onboarding

Procurement Intake Flow (high-level)

1. Requestor fills Procurement Request Form (PRF) with business justification, owner, preferred vendor, cost center, contract term.
2. Procurement reviews PRF within 3 business days and verifies vendor status (new/existing).
3. If vendor is new, Procurement triggers vendor onboarding (W-9, ACH info, security questionnaire if required).
4. Legal review for contracts above threshold or non-standard terms (see Contract Routing rules).
5. Finance approves budget availability and issues PO or triggers invoice routing.
6. Procurement or Requesting Team coordinates delivery and acceptance.

Approval Thresholds (summary)

- One-off purchases <= $10k: Manager approval; standard PRF.
- Recurring subscriptions <= $50k/year: Director approval; Procurement intake + standard terms.
- Recurring subscriptions > $50k/year: VP Finance approval; Legal review + Procurement onboarding.
- Capital expenditure > $100k: CFO approval; Capital request & exec review.

Vendor Security & Privacy

- Any vendor with access to customer data or model artifacts requires a completed Security Questionnaire and Procurement & Security provisioning sign-off before contract signature.
- For private deployments (on-prem/VPC), require SOC2/ISO evidence or written compensating controls.

Contract Intake & Lifecycle

Contract Types Covered

- Customer contracts (TOS, SOWs, Enterprise licenses)
- Third-party vendor contracts (SaaS, hardware, professional services)
- Partner agreements and reseller contracts

Contract Intake Checklist (minimum)

- Business owner and approving cost center
- Contract type and counterparty legal entity
- Commercial terms summary (term length, auto-renew, termination, fees)
- Data handling & security requirements
- Export controls and data residency clauses (if applicable)
- Insurance and indemnity clauses
- Signature authority (see signature matrix)

Contract Review SLAs

- Standard NDAs: Legal review within 2 business days.
- Standard vendor/customer MSAs (no non-standard redlines): Legal & Procurement review within 5 business days.
- Complex or high-risk contracts (custom SOWs, high indemnity): Target 10–15 business days; escalate to Legal Director if beyond 15 days.

Signature Authority Matrix (summary)

- Manager: up to $25k (operational purchases only)
- Director: up to $100k
- VP: up to $500k
- CFO/CEO: > $500k or long-term commitments > 36 months

Contract Repository & Versioning

- All fully executed contracts must be uploaded to the Contract Repository (Finance Drive / Contract DB) within 3 business days of signature, with metadata: counterparty, start/end date, owner, cost center, MSA/SOW links.
- Redline history must be retained. Legal maintains canonical versions.

Revenue Recognition & Billing Policy

Recognition Principles

Redwood recognizes revenue in accordance with ASC 606: identify contract(s), performance obligations, determine transaction price, allocate price to obligations, recognize revenue when obligations satisfied.

Common Scenarios

1. Hosted API (usage-based):
   - Revenue recognized as tokens/usage are delivered; invoiced monthly in arrears.
   - For prepaid commitments (committed monthly/annual), recognize ratably over the period unless deliverables differ.

2. Dedicated or Private (capacity/reserved):
   - For reserved capacity commitments billed periodically, recognize ratably over the contractual period.
   - If installation or on-prem professional services are significant and distinct, treat as separate performance obligations and allocate transaction price accordingly.

3. Professional Services & Onboarding:
   - Recognize based on percentage-of-completion or milestone method when deliverables are distinct and measurable, per Legal/Finance guidance.

Billing & Invoicing Procedures

- Billing cadence: monthly by default, unless counterparty negotiated otherwise (quarterly/annual invoicing allowed for large enterprise deals).
- Invoice contents: contract reference, invoice period, line-level usage or committed units, price, taxes, payment terms, remittance details.
- Standard payment terms: Net 30 unless overridden by Sales Ops and approved by Finance.
- Late payment policy: interest at 1.5% monthly after 30 days; escalate to Revenue Ops for collections after 45 days.

Deferred Revenue & Monthly Close

- Revenue recognition schedule and deferred revenue balances are prepared by Finance each month and reviewed against contract metadata in the Contract Repository.
- Sales credits and customer discounts impacting transaction price must be captured at contract signing and reflected in monthly revenue schedules.

Billing Disputes & Credits

Process

1. Customer raises dispute via billing@redwood.com or assigned AM.
2. Revenue Ops logs dispute and acknowledges within 2 business days.
3. Finance reviews usage records, contract terms, and produces assessment within 7 business days.
4. Agreed credits are issued on next invoice; urgent adjustments may be issued via one-off credit memo.

Audit & Controls

- All revenue-impacting adjustments require dual sign-off (Revenue Ops + Finance Manager).
- Quarterly internal revenue reviews and annual external audit support are mandatory. Documentation for key judgments (allocations, revenue timing) must be stored in Finance audit folder.

Escalation Paths

- Contract or procurement delays interfering with product launches: escalate to Head of Finance and Head of Legal.
- Billing disputes unresolved within 15 business days: escalate to Revenue Ops Director and Sales leadership.

Operational Playbook — Step-by-step Examples

Example: New Vendor with Recurring Subscription (> $50k/year)

1. Requestor completes PRF with vendor and business justification.
2. Procurement validates vendor, requests W-9, and triggers security questionnaire.
3. Legal reviews the vendor MSA; if standard, approves; if not, negotiates key clauses.
4. Finance confirms budget and issues PO tied to cost center.
5. Procurement completes onboarding and notifies Requestor.
6. Vendor invoice routed to AP; Finance matches to PO and processes payment per terms.

Example: Enterprise Customer Contract with Commitment & Professional Services

1. Sales uploads term sheet to Contract Intake and tags Legal & Finance.
2. Legal drafts MSA and SOW; Finance models revenue recognition and billing cadence.
3. Contract review cycle (target 10 business days for negotiations).
4. Signatures captured via e-sign; executed documents uploaded to repository.
5. Billing setup, invoice schedule configured in billing system; revenue schedules created for close.

Templates & Links

- Procurement Request Form (PRF) — Finance Drive link
- Budget template & Forecast workbook — Finance Drive link
- Contract Intake Form & NDA template — Legal Drive link
- Security Questionnaire — Security Drive link
- Invoice template & credit memo form — Revenue Ops folder

KPIs & SLAs

- Procurement PRF initial review SLA: 3 business days.
- Legal review SLA (standard contracts): 5 business days.
- Contract repository upload SLA: 3 business days post-signature.
- Billing dispute acknowledgement: 2 business days.
- Revenue close — monthly schedules published by Finance by 10th business day.

Compliance and Audit Considerations

- Maintain evidence for revenue recognition decisions (contracts, performance obligations mapping, transaction price allocation).
- Ensure procurement records (PRFs, vendor onboarding docs, approvals) are retained per retention policy (7 years for contracts, 3 years for vendor communications unless otherwise required).
